use: Research evidence only. Not a trading signal, not advice, and not used by the live signal path.
title: Research insights: what the evidence supports, and what it does not
headline: 16 claims checked: 3 inconclusive, 7 not supported, 2 suggestive, 4 supported.
caveats: Statuses are assigned by fixed rules from the intervals and counts in the other reports; they are not model opinions.
'Supported' means the sample supports the sign of the effect, not that it is tradeable after costs.
'Suggestive' means a consistent pattern that was selected from several candidates and needs forward confirmation.

provenance.source: derived from the other lab reports (deterministic rules in build_lab_reports.insights)

claims.claim: Bearish Donchian breakouts lose money on the plan simulation
Bullish Donchian breakouts make money on the plan simulation
claims.evidence: mean +0.042 R, 95% CI -0.024 to +0.116; positive in 7 of 9 years

claims.claim: A trend-regime filter (long in uptrend, short in downtrend) improves expectancy
claims.evidence: filtered -0.006 R vs unfiltered -0.018 R; the filtered interval -0.067 to +0.054 contains the unfiltered mean

claims.claim: The choice among the four exit policies changes expectancy
claims.evidence: paired differences vs the fixed-3R exit: A +0.004, B -0.002, C -0.025, D -0.013 (all intervals include zero)

claims.claim: An ML model ranks which breakouts make money
claims.evidence: holdout AUC for R>0 0.5328 (direction-only baseline 0.539); failed gates: holdout_auc, over_direction_baseline, top_decile_lift, plan_profit_auc_within_direction

claims.claim: Breakouts that are less extended in their own direction do better (an avoid-the-extended rule)
claims.evidence: top-minus-bottom quintile spread positive in 8 of 9 years (mean +0.168 R); selected from 7 candidates

claims.claim: Earnings surprises move the price at the release
A tradeable drift follows large positive earnings surprises
claims.evidence: 20-day market-adjusted drift after the reaction -0.16%, 95% CI -0.46% to +0.15%

claims.claim: A recent positive earnings surprise improves a bullish Donchian breakout
claims.evidence: +0.031 R after a surprise vs +0.037 R without

claims.claim: SEC-detected recurring operating improvements are followed by a larger price reaction than ordinary earnings
claims.evidence: reaction +2.22% (n=1,544) vs -0.51% without an anomaly (n=6,270); positive in 10 of 10 years

claims.claim: A tradeable drift follows SEC-detected recurring operating improvements
claims.evidence: 20-day drift after the reaction -0.10%, 95% CI -0.85% to +0.69%

claims.claim: The market reacts less to net-income jumps without an operating move (suspected one-time) than to recurring operating improvements
A recent recurring-operating catalyst improves a bullish Donchian breakout (fixed-3R exit, net of costs)
claims.evidence: +0.155 R (n=1,194, CI -0.136 to +0.437) vs +0.085 R with no recent earnings (n=44,547)

claims.claim: Within recurring-operating catalysts a different exit policy beats the fixed-3R exit
claims.evidence: the fixed-3R exit is itself the best policy (+0.155 R); the others range +0.052 to +0.080 R, all intervals overlap

claims.claim: Financial-anomaly features predict how large the reaction will be beyond trailing volatility
claims.evidence: AUC 0.7016 vs trailing volatility alone 0.6986 (chronological test from 2022-02-15)

claims.claim: Financial-anomaly features predict the direction of the reaction
claims.evidence: AUC 0.5629 vs best single-metric baseline 0.5456 (chronological test); modest lift on a coin-flip base rate 0.5064
